Bug_Details:
Using \s anywhere except at the end of a line in a text block is potentially misleading. When Java introduced text blocks as a feature, it also introduced a new string
escape sequence \s. This escape sequence is another way to write a normal
space, but it has the advantage that it can be used at the end of a line in a
text block, where a normal space would be stripped. This new escape sequence can easily be confused with the regex \s, which is a
metacharacter that matches any kind of whitespace character. To write that
metacharacter in a Java string, you must still write \\s: an escaped backslash
followed by an s. There is little reason to ever write the Java escape \s except at the end of a
line. Either use a normal space, or switch to \\s if you are trying to write
the regex metacharacter. // Each line here is five characters long.
String colors = """
    one \s
    two \s
    three
    """; // Each line here is five characters long.
String colors = """
    one \s
    two \s
    three
    """;
Bug_Explanation: The bug is demonstrated by using the \s escape sequence in the middle of lines inside a text block. This is potentially misleading because \s is meant to represent a normal space at the end of a line in a text block, rather than as a whitespace character in the middle of the line.
Trigger_Explanation: The test case triggers the bug by comparing the expected output with the actual output from the `showBug` method. The use of `\s` inside the text block in the original class is misleading and results in an unexpected string output, causing the assert to fail.
